elements.element: Governing law is the laws of the State of New York
elements.evidence: "governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York"

elements.element: Exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County
elements.evidence: "The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction"

elements.element: Governing law and forum form a permitted corresponding pair
elements.evidence: NY law in § 28.1 paired with NY County courts in § 28.2; conflicting Singapore law/forum deleted

elements.element: Governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales
elements.evidence: "the laws of the State of New York" — preferred law, not a fallback alternative

elements.element: Courts of Delaware, California, or London
elements.evidence: "courts located in New York County, New York"

offending_extra_words: temporary injunctive relief in those courts to protect
reasons: Preferred level is complete: § 28.1 now specifies New York law and § 28.2 retains exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts of New York County, a permitted corresponding pair, and the conflicting Singapore law/forum sentence is fully removed.
Fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (no Delaware, California, or England and Wales law/forum), which is irrelevant since the locked target is preferred and preferred is met.

Minimality fails: the second operation narrowing the interim-relief carve-out from "another court with jurisdiction" to "those courts" was not needed to achieve New York law and New York County exclusive jurisdiction; the single § 28.1 replacement sufficed.

The narrowing also strips Customer of the practical ability to seek emergency injunctive relief where infringement or a confidentiality breach occurs, and leaves a sentence that merely restates the exclusive-forum clause (redundant but not contradictory).
Untouched terms (personal jurisdiction submission, venue/forum waiver, Confidential Information definition) remain effective; no undefined term is introduced.
